title: Guitarists, bands and Willie Dixon's Big Three in Chicago
summary: Slim names guitar players, describes his small bands and says blues drew the work when Dixon came in.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, I'm going to tell you. I didn't know too much about. I know the guitar players. I'm going to tell you about the guitar players. The only guitar players I have in there. What's that bright boy's name, man? What's that bright boy named Walter? What used to? Willoughby? Was that his name? Willoughby? Yeah. Willoughby? Now, wait a minute. Him and Buddy Doris. Guitar players in the car. How do you know what? What's that? I'm saying. I'm on the drum. I don't know what I'm about. That's Willoughby. Guitar players. But Robert Johnson. Willoughby. I didn't know Robert Junior that day when you started. No.
Robert Junior wasn't even talking about, did you?

You wasn't talking about. Willoughby. Buddy Doris. And, uh, and Blind Boy fellow. And, uh, who else was there? We always used horns. Yeah. Trumpets. In that time, you played by yourself mostly. Little local fellows. Yes. Fellows like a band. You know how the band. And, uh, you know. Well, I mean, I had to go out to play for a day. And for some. I had trampone and sax. Drums. Yeah, I never did have upright bass. Them were drums. Oh. I played there in Chicago. Fifteen years. Trill. Which he got there. And take the name of it. Now my trill was named Playboy. I learned his Playboy. Guitar, drumming, you know. And just me on the piano. And we was cutting them good, too. Because Dixon had the Big Three and I had to play for it. And, well, he was, Dixon started out at the playing. And I don't know what year. I, listen, you used to fool with the blues. You know, he didn't fool with the blues. See, that time.
He didn't know. He didn't know.

He was dominating the blues. When he came in, the blues was getting all the work. Because they kept the house packed. Because the blues was Arkansas, Mississippi, Georgia, Florida. And all the time they mix it up. That's the way. They know what I'm saying. A whole lot of...
I was going anywhere. I'd been fouling about something. Because they were too loud. It's a million times, I don't know. But I was trying to find that here.
